section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports a single community study (Study X) of 509 men in London, United Kingdom, examining links between the Big Five personality traits and body image measures, including drive for muscularity and body appreciation. Hierarchical regressions (controlling for BMI and subjective social status) found Neuroticism positively predicted drive for muscularity and Neuroticism (negatively) and Extraversion (positively) predicted body appreciation; no instrument names, demographic breakdowns (age, race, education), or BMI means/correlations were provided.
section_summary.evidence_source: "The present study examined associations between the Big Five personality domains and measures of men's body image. A total of 509 men from the community in London, UK, completed measures of drive for muscularity, body appreciation, the Big Five domains, and subjective social status, and provided their demographic details." and "once the effects of participant body mass index (BMI) and subjective social status had been accounted for, men's body appreciation was significantly predicted by Neuroticism (ˇ = −.35) and Extraversion (ˇ = .12)."
